title: Last Orders
tagline: Where the trains have gone, the railway names stayed: of the 127 railway-named pubs more than a kilometre from any working line, 105 stand nearer the lifted trackbed than the pub next door.
blurb: Every named pub in Great Britain (38,986 of them, from OpenStreetMap) taken apart into the slots its name is built from, colour and animal, trade and Arms, A and B, and measured against every railway and canal on the ground. Railway is the sixth commonest pub name in the country. The test that was meant to prove railway names remember dead lines failed: railway pubs sit even closer to lines that still run, because a Station Hotel stands by a station. So the working railways were taken out of the picture: among pubs more than a kilometre from any open line, the railway-named one is nearer the old trackbed than its neighbour in 105 of 127 pairs, 82 of 96 using only the words Railway and Station, while Red Lions and White Harts in the same country show no pull at all.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap, Great Britain extract from Geofabrik (great-britain-latest.osm.pbf, 2.1 GB, downloaded 2026-10-05): every pub, and every railway and canal, open or disused. © OpenStreetMap contributors.
